original_question: In the polynomial tuning construction, does the resulting polynomial depend continuously on P2?
target_in_paper: §2. Quasiconformal Surgery (Douady, Bielefeld, Shishikura), tuning subsection, Question 6: "Does the resulting polynomial vary continuously with P2?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the tuning construction in §2 and the specific continuity problem with respect to the second input polynomial P2. It is already very close to the paper’s official Question 6, and it does not drift into the neighboring mating or intertwining continuity questions.
missing_details: The paper is about complex polynomials in one variable z, not arbitrary polynomials.
P1 is not arbitrary: it must have a periodic critical point ω of period k, and no other critical points may lie in the entire basin of the corresponding superattracting cycle.
P2 is not arbitrary: it must have one critical point whose local degree matches the degree d of the critical point ω.
The nearby setup assumes that the Julia sets of both P1 and P2 are connected.

For the explicit tuning description used immediately before Question 6, the closure of the immediate basin of ω is assumed homeomorphic to the closed unit disk, and J(P2) is assumed locally connected.
When d > 2, the construction depends on choosing one of the d-1 possible conjugating homeomorphisms between P1^k on the immediate basin and z -> z^d on the disk.
The question presupposes the existence issue raised just before it: the topological tuning must actually yield something conjugate to a polynomial of the same degree as P1.

The phrase 'depend continuously on P2' is not fully stand-alone unless one specifies the sense of continuity; the paper leaves the topology/normalization implicit, so the safest self-contained formulation is continuity of the resulting polynomial up to conjugacy.
refined_question: Fix a complex polynomial P1 with a periodic critical point ω of period k, assume that no other critical points lie in the full basin of the associated superattracting cycle, and let d be the local degree of ω. Let P2 be a complex polynomial with one critical point of degree d, and assume that J(P1) and J(P2) are connected; in the explicit tuning setup described in §2, also assume that the closure of the immediate basin of ω is homeomorphic to the closed unit disk and that J(P2) is locally connected, with one of the possible conjugacies to z -> z^d chosen when d > 2. Whenever the tuning construction produces a polynomial P3 of degree deg(P1), called P1 tuned with P2 at ω, does the resulting tuned polynomial P3, regarded up to conjugacy, vary continuously as P2 varies?
justification: The draft is targeting the tuning subsection of §2, not the mating continuity question (Question 3) and not the intertwining continuity question (Question 11). The exact official target is Question 6 on page 5. To make that question stand alone, one must import the hypotheses stated in the tuning setup on pages 4-5: the special periodic critical point ω of P1, the restriction on other critical points, the condition on P2 having one critical point of matching degree, connectedness of the two Julia sets, and the additional assumptions used in the explicit topological construction. The preceding Question 4 is also relevant because Question 6 only makes sense once the tuning is known to produce a polynomial. The paper itself does not formalize the topology for continuity, so phrasing the question in terms of the resulting polynomial up to conjugacy stays closest to the paper’s intent without broadening it.
